blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Continuous diffusion language models generate all tokens in parallel, yet high-quality generation can still require hundreds of network evaluations (NFEs). We study how distributional distillation can reduce this cost by exploiting the student’s probabilistic token outputs. Our unified formulation connects the student’s output parameterization to the resulting gradient estimators and yields two methods with the same student architecture and reverse-KL matching objective: Simplex-DMD uses continuous token relaxations and pathwise gradients, while Reinforce-DMD uses categorical sampling and REINFORCE with a learned density ratio. We develop both methods for multi-step generation and investigate the training and sampling choices associated with each parameterization. On OpenWebText, for sequences of 1,024 tokens, Simplex-DMD achieves a generative perplexity of 45.6 at a unigram entropy of 5.44 nats in just 4 NFEs, a 49% reduction relative to the strongest evaluated diffusion baseline at matched entropy and sampling budget. Reinforce-DMD improves the frontier at larger budgets, reaching a generative perplexity of 14.9 at an entropy of 5.00 nats with 256 NFEs, a 20% reduction under the same comparison protocol.
blocks.zh: 持续的传播语言模型会同时生成出所有符号,然而高品质的生成仍然需要数百个网络评价(NFEs). 我们研究如何利用学生的概率标志性产出来减少这种成本。 我们的统一配方将学生的输出参数化与结果的梯度估计器连接起来,并产生两种方法与同样的学生架构和倒向-KL匹配目标:Simlex-DMD使用连续的符号放松和走道梯度,而加强-DMD则使用绝对的采样和有学习密度比的REINFORCE. 我们为多步骤生成制定两种方法,并调查与每个参数化有关的培训和取样选择。 在OpenWebText上,对于1,024个令牌的序列,Simlex-DMD在仅4个NFE中的5.44纳特的单倍体上,实现了45.6的基因通透性,相对于相应的等效和采样预算中最强的经评价的传播基线,下降49%. 强化DMD在更大的预算上改进了前沿,在有256个非FEs的5.00纳特的 en上达到14.9分基因的复杂度,在同一比较协议下减少20%。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en:
Diffusion language models generate text either through diffusion directly in discrete token space ( Austin et al., 2021 ; Lou et al., 2024 ; Sahoo et al., 2024 ) or through Gaussian diffusion in a continuous embedding space ( Dieleman et al., 2022 ) .
Recent advances in continuous diffusion language models have shown that the latter approach is competitive
with its discrete counterparts ( Chen et al., 2026b ; Yang et al., 2026 ; Hu et al., 2026 ) .
Although both approaches update all sequence positions in parallel,
generating high-quality text can still require hundreds of sequential network evaluations.
This sampling cost motivates diffusion distillation, which aims to reduce the number of evaluations
while preserving generation quality, using a pretrained teacher to supervise a student to generate samples in fewer steps.

持续传播语言模式的最新进展表明,后者具有竞争力。

生成高质量的文本仍需要数百个连续的网络评价。

blocks.en: Two broad approaches differ in the teacher supervision they provide. Trajectory-based methods supervise student predictions or transitions along the teacher’s dynamics. For continuous data, these include consistency and flow map methods ( Song et al., 2023 ; Boffi et al., 2025b ) , and for discrete data they have been developed for both discrete and continuous diffusion models ( Deschenaux & Gulcehre, 2025 ; Hayakawa et al., 2025 ; Roos et al., 2026 ; Potaptchik et al., 2026 ; Lee et al., 2026 ) .
blocks.zh: 两种广泛的方法在教师监督方面各不相同。 基于轨迹的方法监督学生的预测或沿教师动态的过渡. 对于连续数据,这些包括一致性和流图方法(Song等人,2023年;Boffi等人,2025年b),对于离散和连续扩散模型,已开发出离散数据(Dechenaux & Gulcehre,2025年;Hayakawa等人,2025年;Roos等人,2026年;Potaptchik等人,2026年;Lee等人,2026年)。

blocks.en: Distributional methods instead use the teacher to guide the student toward the data distribution, without prescribing its generation trajectories. Developed for continuous data in both one-step and multi-step regimes ( Luo et al., 2023 ; Yin et al., 2024 ; Salimans et al., 2024 ) , these approaches have recently been explored for discrete data, like language, with discrete ( Hoogeboom et al., 2026 ; Li et al., 2026 ; Zhu et al., 2025 ) and continuous diffusion models ( Chen et al., 2026a ) .
blocks.zh: 相反,分配方法使用教师指导学生向数据分配方向发展,而没有规定其生成轨迹。 为单步制和多步制的连续数据(Luo等人,2023年;Yin等人,2024年;Salimans等人,2024年)开发了这些方法,最近为语言等离散数据(Hoogeboom等人,2026年;Li等人,2026年;Zhu等人,2025年)和连续传播模型(Chen等人,2026年a年)进行了探索。 。 。 。 。

blocks.en:
We study distributional distillation for continuous diffusion models on discrete data (CDMd). Their denoising networks predict a probability distribution over clean tokens at each position, given noisy embeddings and a noise level. Retaining these outputs for the student leaves a natural choice: use the probability vectors directly as continuous token representations, or sample discrete tokens from them.
In both cases, we embed and noise the student outputs and match their distribution to the corresponding noised data distribution under a reverse-KL objective. These two parameterizations yield different training procedures. Simplex Distribution Matching Distillation (Simplex-DMD) uses pathwise gradients through continuous token relaxations, with an auxiliary denoiser estimating the score of the noised student distribution, following Diff-Instruct and DMD ( Luo et al., 2023 ; Yin et al., 2024 ) . REINFORCE Distribution Matching Distillation (Reinforce-DMD) uses categorical samples and a REINFORCE estimator ( Williams, 1992 ) , with a discriminator estimating the density ratio between noised student and data distributions.
We extend both methods to multi-step generation and study their training behavior and quality-diversity tradeoffs across sampling budgets.
blocks.zh:

在这两种情况下,我们都会嵌入和噪声学生产出,并将其分布与逆-KL目标下的相应噪声数据分布相匹配。 这两个参数化产生不同的培训程序. Simplex Distruction Matching Districtation(Simplex-DMD)通过连续的令牌放松使用有路径的梯度,辅助denoiser估计了继Diff-Instruct和DMD(Luo等,2023;Yin等,2024)之后的点名生分布分. REINFORCE 分布相匹配分解(Reinforce-DMD)使用绝对的样本和一个REINFORCE 估计器(Williams, 1992),其中歧视者估计了噪声学生和数据分布的密度比.

blocks.en:
Our contributions are as follows: ∙ \bullet We introduce a unified framework for distributional distillation that compares noised student and data distributions
through a generic discrepancy. This formulation recovers objectives used in prior work as particular choices of discrepancy
and extends to multi-step generation. ∙ \bullet We specialize this framework to reverse-KL matching and derive two distillation methods: Simplex-DMD and Reinforce-DMD. Together, they provide continuous-relaxation and categorical-sampling approaches to training the same student architecture for multi-step generation. ∙ \bullet We distill the same LangFlow teacher ( Chen et al., 2026b ) (170M parameters) with both methods and evaluate generation of 1,024-token sequences on OpenWebText using generative perplexity–entropy frontiers ( Pynadath et al., 2026 ) . The methods improve on the evaluated baselines at complementary sampling budgets: Simplex-DMD at 2–16 network evaluations and Reinforce-DMD at 256 evaluations, matching the best baseline at 128 ( Figure 1 ). At four evaluations and unigram entropy 5.44, Simplex-DMD reduces Gen PPL from 90.2 for ReDi to 45.6; at 256 evaluations and entropy 5.00, Reinforce-DMD reduces it from 18.6 for D-MMD to 14.9.

blocks.en: 3 Distribution matching distillation for continuous diffusion on discrete data
blocks.zh: 3 分布相匹配蒸馏,以便在离散数据上持续扩散

blocks.en:
Distributional distillation trains a student by matching the distribution
of its generated samples to the data distribution. In our setting,
the student takes as input a latent Z T Z_{T} at noise level T ∈ ( 0 , 1 ] T\in(0,1] and produces a
distribution over clean token representations. These outputs are then
renoised with the Gaussian forward process of Section 2 , and
their distributions are matched with the corresponding data marginals p t p_{t} at lower noise levels t < T t<T . For the approaches considered, the matching objective involves
the fixed pretrained CDMd p θ p^{\theta} , used as the distillation teacher.

More precisely, given Z T = z T Z_{T}=z_{T} , the student network outputs 𝐱 η ​ ( z T , T ) ∈ Δ K L \mathbf{x}^{\eta}(z_{T},T)\in\Delta_{K}^{L} , which parameterizes a conditional
kernel 𝗄 T η ( ⋅ ∣ z T ) \mathsf{k}_{T}^{\eta}(\cdot\mid z_{T}) . We consider two parameterizations
of this kernel. The first uses the probability vectors themselves as
simplex-valued token representations, while the second samples one
categorical token at each sequence position: 𝗄 T η ​ ( d ​ 𝐱 ∣ z T ) = δ 𝐱 η ​ ( z T , T ) ​ ( d ​ 𝐱 ) , 𝐱 ∈ Δ K L , \displaystyle\mathsf{k}_{T}^{\eta}(\mathrm{d}\mathbf{x}\mid z_{T})=\delta_{\mathbf{x}^{\eta}(z_{T},T)}(\mathrm{d}\mathbf{x}),\quad\mathbf{x}\in\Delta_{K}^{L}, (continuous relaxation) , \displaystyle\quad\text{(continuous relaxation)}, (6) 𝗄 T η ​ ( 𝐱 ∣ z T ) = ∏ ℓ = 1 L ⟨ 𝐱 ℓ , 𝐱 η , ℓ ​ ( z T , T ) ⟩ , 𝐱 ∈ 𝖷 , \displaystyle\mathsf{k}_{T}^{\eta}(\mathbf{x}\mid z_{T})=\prod_{\ell=1}^{L}\left\langle\mathbf{x}^{\ell},\mathbf{x}^{\eta,\ell}(z_{T},T)\right\rangle,\quad\mathbf{x}\in\mathsf{X}, (discrete sampling) . \displaystyle\quad\text{(discrete sampling)}. (7) These two parameterizations share the same distribution-matching objective
but lead to different gradient estimators.
We formulate this objective for one-step generation in a framework unifying existing methods by considering a general class of matching objectives,
extend it to multi-step generation and derive
Simplex-DMD for the continuous relaxation and Reinforce-DMD for discrete sampling.

blocks.en: 3.1 A unified view of one-step distribution matching
blocks.zh: 3.1 国家 单步分布匹配的统一视图

blocks.en:
We first consider one-step generation and isolate a common formulation of
distributional distillation. Existing distribution-matching methods can be
viewed as comparing the noised student and data distributions across noise
levels, while differing in the discrepancy used to compare these marginals.
We formalize this view through a generic discrepancy 𝖣 \mathsf{D} , before
specializing it to the reverse KL used by our methods.

blocks.en: 3.5 Related work
blocks.zh: 3.5 相关工作

blocks.en:
Diffusion-LM jointly learns embeddings and a diffusion model ( Li et al., 2022 ) , SED uses self-conditioning in embedding diffusion ( Strudel et al., 2022 ) , and Plaid develops a likelihood-based training framework ( Gulrajani & Hashimoto, 2023 ) .
Alongside these developments, CDCD introduced score interpolation, parameterizing the score through an estimate of the posterior mean ( Dieleman et al., 2022 ) .
More recently, LangFlow ( Chen et al., 2026b ) and RePlaid ( Yang et al., 2026 ) refined noise scheduling and training, achieving language modeling performance competitive with that of discrete diffusion models.
blocks.zh:
传播-LM联合学习嵌入和扩散模型(Li等,2022年),SED在嵌入扩散中采用自调节(Strudl等,2022年),而Plaid开发出基于可能性的训练框架(Gulrajani和桥本,2023年).
除了这些发展外,CDCD还引入了分数内插法,通过后期平均值估算参数化分数(Dieleman等,2022年).
最近,LangFlow(Chen等,2026年b)和RePlaid(Yang等,2026年)对噪声排行和培训进行了精细化,实现了语言模型化性能与离散扩散模型相竞争.

blocks.en:
Consistency models learn to map states along a probability-flow trajectory to a common endpoint, enabling generation with one or a few model evaluations ( Song et al., 2023 ; Song & Dhariwal, 2024 ) . Flow map matching generalizes this construction to maps between arbitrary times, with objectives for distilling pretrained models as well as training directly from data through self-distillation ( Boffi et al., 2025a ; Boffi et al., 2025b ) . Categorical flow maps , including CFM ( Roos et al., 2026 ) , DFM ( Potaptchik et al., 2026 ) , and FMLM ( Lee et al., 2026 ) , build on CDMd to extend these ideas to discrete data, enabling one- and few-step generation.
For discrete diffusion, SDTT matches predictions along teacher rollouts ( Deschenaux & Gulcehre, 2025 ) , while Di4C distills transition compositions into mixture models that capture correlations across dimensions ( Hayakawa et al., 2025 ) .
A complementary approach is taken by Rectified Flow ( Liu et al., 2023 ) and a discrete adaptation ReDi ( Yoo et al., 2025 ) , which iteratively rectifies the source-target coupling in flow matching to accelerate sampling.
blocks.zh:
一致性模型学习将概率-流轨迹的状态映射到共同的终点,使生成能够进行一到几个模型评价(Song等,2023;Song & Dhariwal,2024). 流程图将这一构图归纳为任意时间之间的地图,目标是通过自沉直接从数据中提炼出预先训练过的模型并进行培训(Boffi等,2025a;Boffi等,2025b)。 分类流程图,包括CFM(Roos等,2026年),DFM (Potaptchik等,2026年),以及FMLM(Lee等,2026年),以CDMd为基础,将这些想法推广到离散的数据上,使单步和几步生成成为可能.
对于离散扩散,SDTT在教师推广时与预测相匹配(Dechenaux & Gulcehre, 2025年),而Di4C将过渡成分分馏成能够捕捉到不同维度间关联的混合物模型(Hayakawa等人,2025年)。
采用补充方法的有:经校正的流量(Liu等人,2023年)和离散的ReDi(Yoo等人,2025年),它们反复地调整了源-目标相匹配的流量相接,以加速采样。

blocks.en:
We evaluate whether Simplex-DMD and Reinforce-DMD preserve generation quality and diversity
when distilling a continuous diffusion language model to reduced sampling
budgets. We compare them with diffusion and distillation baselines across
network evaluation budgets, and ablate the main training and sampling choices.

We evaluate generation quality with generative perplexity (Gen PPL, lower is better), computed
by GPT-2 Large, and diversity with unigram entropy (higher is better). Since lower perplexity can
result from reduced diversity, we compare Gen PPL–entropy frontiers obtained
by varying the sampling temperature ( Pynadath et al., 2026 ) . Baselines include
the LangFlow teacher, the continuous-diffusion distillation method FMLM,

blocks.en:
We detail the design choices made to obtain the results presented in the previous subsection,
and the related ablations validating them.

blocks.en:
Teacher supervision stabilizes Reinforce-DMD. Figure 3 examines the effect of the teacher KL anchor introduced in
( 21 ) at NFE = 128 \mathrm{NFE}=128 . Removing the anchor ( β = 0 \beta=0 ) leads to collapse,
with essentially zero unigram entropy. Positive anchor weights and an annealed schedule prevent
collapse and yield similar generative perplexity–entropy frontiers, with β = 0.5 \beta=0.5 providing a
modest improvement over the other tested settings. These results indicate that teacher supervision is
needed for stable Reinforce-DMD training in the tested configurations, while performance is relatively insensitive
to the anchor weight within the positive range considered. We therefore use β = 0.5 \beta=0.5 in our default configuration.

blocks.en:
Further ablations in Sections E.3 and E.5 support the remaining
choices of our default configuration. Initializing the student from scratch
leads to collapse in the tested configurations, motivating initialization
from the teacher. Self-conditioning improves Simplex-DMD but provides no benefit for Reinforce-DMD in our
experiments, so we use it only for Simplex-DMD.
For Simplex-DMD, a bridge-based training construction
inspired by moment matching ( Salimans et al., 2024 ) underperforms the
forward-renoising training objective; we discuss its auxiliary score
approximation in Section D.4 .

blocks.en: 5 Conclusion
blocks.zh: 5 结论

blocks.en:
We introduced a distribution-matching framework for distilling continuous
diffusion models on discrete data and derived two methods from a common
reverse-KL objective: Simplex-DMD, based on simplex-valued outputs and pathwise
gradients, and Reinforce-DMD, based on categorical sampling and score-function
estimation. On OpenWebText, they improve generation at complementary sampling
budgets, with Simplex-DMD strongest at low budgets and Reinforce-DMD at larger budgets among
the evaluated distillation methods. Like other distribution-matching
approaches, our methods require a pretrained teacher and an auxiliary model
during training. Our experiments are also limited to academic model scale;
scaling to substantially larger language models will require studying this
training overhead and extending evaluation beyond the Gen PPL–entropy
protocol used here.

These objectives also put different pressures on learned embeddings.
The diffusion term alone vanishes if all token embeddings coincide,
whereas cross-entropy favors distinguishable tokens and can encourage
increasing their separation relative to the noise. To control this scale,
embeddings are constrained to a sphere, with each row of 𝐄 \mathbf{E} having
norm 1 1 or d \sqrt{d} , where d d is the embedding dimension ( Dieleman et al., 2022 ; Chen et al., 2026b ; Yang et al., 2026 ) .
This prevents the embedding norms from vanishing or diverging, although
normalization alone does not prevent different tokens from sharing the
same embedding.

blocks.en: E.1 Implementation details

blocks.en:
Table 3 separates teacher pretraining from the
additional updates used to train the distilled students.
Both the student and auxiliary models retain the LangFlow architecture ( Chen et al., 2026b ) ; we use an embedding-space diffusion transformer with 12 12 blocks,
hidden dimension 768 768 , 12 12 attention heads and rotary position embeddings, conditioned on the
noise level through adaLN modulation, with an output head over the vocabulary that is not tied to 𝐄 \mathbf{E} .
Each network has 170.8 170.8 M parameters, of which the 38.6 38.6 M of 𝐄 \mathbf{E} are frozen and shared with the teacher.
For Reinforce-DMD, the discriminator keeps this trunk and replaces the vocabulary head with a scalar output per position.
Optimization-step counts alone do not imply equal training compute:
batch sizes and the number of network evaluations per update can differ,
and our methods alternate auxiliary and student updates.
Each student is trained for 10,000 10{,}000 optimizer updates in total, comprising 8,000 8{,}000 auxiliary updates and 2,000 2{,}000 student updates.
Our training GPU budget comprises four nodes with eight NVIDIA H100 GPUs each ( 32 32 GPUs in total).

blocks.en:
The Reinforce-DMD discriminator uses the same transformer backbone as the teacher, including rotary positional embeddings and noise-level conditioning through adaptive layer normalization.
It operates directly on noised latents in the teacher’s embedding space, omitting the token-embedding layer and replacing the vocabulary prediction head with a scalar head.
We initialize the backbone from the teacher checkpoint and initialize the scalar head separately.
The head applies noise-conditioned adaptive layer normalization followed by a projection to one logit per position; averaging these logits over sequence positions yields a single scalar logit per sequence.

强化DMD歧视者使用与老师相同的变压器骨干,包括通过适应地层正常化来进行回转位置嵌入和噪声水平调节.
它直接运行在老师嵌入空间中的噪声潜想上,省略了装入符号的地层并用平板头来取而代之的词汇预测头.
我们从教师检查站初始化骨干,并分别初始化了斯卡尔头.
头部采用有噪声条件的适应层正常化,然后对每个位置的一个对数进行预测;平均这些对数相对于序列位置,每个序列产生一个单一的分级对数。

We use n aux = 4 n_{\mathrm{aux}}=4 : four auxiliary updates on detached student samples, followed by one student update.
At each optimization step, we sample the time pair ( t , T ) ∼ ν (t,T)\sim\nu .

Generative perplexity is computed by exponentiating the mean token negative log-likelihood under GPT-2-large.
We evaluate with a single random seed, as in the default experimental setup of Gourevitch et al. (2026, Appendix I.1) .
We pair perplexity with diversity measured as the mean per-sequence Shannon entropy of empirical GPT-2 token frequencies, in nats, to obtain a quality–diversity frontier at each sampling budget, following Pynadath et al. (2026) .

Figure 7 compares the three as Simplex-DMD training variants. They do not move the frontier;
they move the temperature- 1.0 1.0 point along it. At both budgets, the sampled-token target reaches the lowest
Gen PPL, but at the lowest entropy of the three, and squared error sits
at the opposite end, more diverse and less fluent, with the soft target between them.
The variants also differ in how fast entropy erodes: from NFE = 32 \mathrm{NFE}=32 to NFE = 128 \mathrm{NFE}=128 the soft target loses 1.03 1.03 nats of unigram entropy against 1.06 1.06 for squared error and 1.17 1.17 for the sampled-token target. Since Gen PPL falls with entropy along this frontier, a variant that
collapses faster reports the better perplexity while generating less diverse text. We keep
the soft target for that reason.
